name: Chris Bittle
current_role: MP for St. Catharines (re-elected 2025, 52%). Chair of Standing Committee on Procedure and House Affairs (45th Parliament). Previously Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Canadian Heritage, then Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Housing, Infrastructure and Communities.

controversies.title: Bill C-11 witness intimidation allegations (2022)
controversies.details: As Parliamentary Secretary for Heritage, Bittle sent a letter to the Lobbying Commissioner requesting an investigation into Digital First Canada and its executive director Scott Benzie, who testified against Bill C-11 (Online Streaming Act). The letter was filed months earlier but leaked to coincide with Benzie's appearance before the Senate committee. Multiple senators condemned the tactic as witness intimidation. Senator Don Plett said he was 'disgusted' by Bittle's actions. Senator Housakos raised formal concerns about intimidation of parliamentary witnesses.

controversies.title: Hostile treatment of Meta witnesses at Heritage Committee (2023)
controversies.details: During Bill C-18 (Online News Act) hearings, Bittle accused a Meta representative of being untruthful and evasive, threatening to refer her responses to the law clerk. Critics characterized his conduct as aggressive and intimidating toward tech industry witnesses.

controversies.title: Indigenous creator gaslighting allegations (2022)
controversies.details: First Nations witness Vanessa Brousseau testified before a Senate committee that she was subject to intimidation and gaslighting from the federal government after voicing concerns about Bill C-11.

lobbying_highlights: 379 total lobbying contacts logged in the federal Lobbyists Registration System

As Parliamentary Secretary for Canadian Heritage, served as key government point person on Bills C-11 (Online Streaming Act) and C-18 (Online News Act), both heavily lobbied pieces of legislation involving telecom, tech, and media industry interests
maid_position: Voted YES on Bill C-14 (2016, original MAID legislation) and YES on Bill C-7 (2021, MAID expansion). Publicly stated he 'fully supports permitting advance consent' for MAID where death is reasonably foreseeable.
foreign_connections: No publicly documented foreign government connections or sponsored foreign travel found in available public records
financial_notes: Travel expenditure reports publicly available through House of Commons Proactive Disclosure portal (ourcommons.ca)
No Ethics Commissioner findings or sanctions found in public record

name: Wayne Long
riding: Saint John-Kennebecasis, New Brunswick (formerly Saint John-Rothesay)
current_role: MP for Saint John-Kennebecasis (re-elected 2025, 58%, 4th term). Secretary of State responsible for Canada Revenue Agency and Financial Institutions (appointed 2025).

controversies.title: Removed from two parliamentary committees for breaking party ranks (2017)
controversies.details: Long was kicked off the Standing Committee on Human Resources and the Standing Committee on Access to Information, Privacy and Ethics after supporting a Conservative motion to extend consultation on proposed small business tax changes. He publicly opposed the Liberal government's tax reform, citing the large concentration of small businesses in his riding.

controversies.title: Anti-Palestinian remarks at Gaza solidarity protest (December 2023)
controversies.details: Video emerged of Long arguing with Palestine solidarity protesters outside a Liberal Party holiday event in Saint John. His staffer Jeannette Arsenault accused protesters of 'believing in terrorism.' Long later stated his words were 'hurtful and inappropriate' and apologized. Independent Jewish Voices NB called for a Liberal Party investigation and his resignation. Palestinian and Jewish Unity (PAJU) also called for his resignation.

controversies.title: Continued confrontations with Palestine solidarity activists (2024)
controversies.details: Despite his initial apology, Long continued to issue allegations against individuals in what activists described as attempts to discredit and intimidate Palestinian solidarity protesters. A July 2024 incident at a Saint John waterfront park event was documented on video. A Change.org petition demanded accountability from Long for 'unethical conduct.'

controversies.title: Called for SNC-Lavalin investigation against own party (2019)
controversies.details: Long broke ranks with the Liberal Party again by calling for a 'full and transparent investigation' into alleged PMO interference in the SNC-Lavalin prosecution, joining opposition calls for the House of Commons Justice Committee to investigate after Jody Wilson-Raybould's allegations.

lobbying_highlights: 378 total lobbying contacts logged in the federal Lobbyists Registration System
Now serves as Secretary of State for CRA and Financial Institutions, a role with significant exposure to financial industry lobbying
maid_position: Voted YES on Bill C-14 (2016, original MAID legislation) and YES on Bill C-7 (2021, MAID expansion).
foreign_connections: No publicly documented foreign government connections found in available public records
Confrontations with Gaza solidarity activists and staffer's comments about terrorism drew accusations of pro-Israel bias from Palestinian advocacy groups
financial_notes: No Ethics Commissioner findings or sanctions found in public record
Travel expenditure reports publicly available through House of Commons Proactive Disclosure portal

name: Bardish Chagger
current_role: MP for Waterloo (re-elected 2025, 60%, 4th term). Former Government House Leader (2016-2019), Former Minister of Diversity, Inclusion and Youth (2019-2021). Former Chair of Standing Committee on Procedure and House Affairs (2021-2024). Currently backbench MP.

controversies.title: WE Charity scandal - signed $43.5 million sole-sourced contract (2020)
controversies.details: As Minister of Diversity, Inclusion and Youth, Chagger signed the sole-sourced contract awarding WE Charity up to $43.53 million to administer the Canada Student Service Grant (CSSG) program. Originally reported as $19.5 million, the true value was revealed during her testimony before the House of Commons Finance Committee on July 16, 2020. The breakdown: $19.5M base payment, $10.5M for smaller non-profits, $13.53M for additional volunteer placements. Chagger had met with WE Charity days before PM Trudeau announced the program. She was the first government witness to testify. She claimed the civil service recommended WE Charity, not the PMO. WE Charity had documented ties to PM Trudeau and Finance Minister Morneau's families.

controversies.title: Refused to resign over WE Charity role (2020)
controversies.details: Despite being the minister who signed the contract and met with WE Charity before the announcement, Chagger publicly stated she would not resign. NDP documents showed she was a 'key driver' in the WE Charity decision. She was subsequently removed from cabinet in the 2021 reshuffle.

controversies.title: Stepped down as PROC chair (2024)
controversies.details: Chagger unexpectedly resigned as chair of the influential Procedure and House Affairs Committee (PROC) on April 29, 2024, after holding the position since December 2021. She cited wanting to 'fight for constituents' voices' in Waterloo.

lobbying_highlights: 350 total lobbying contacts logged in the federal Lobbyists Registration System
As Minister of Diversity, Inclusion and Youth, was responsible for programs attracting significant lobbying activity including the CSSG that led to the WE Charity scandal
As former Government House Leader (2016-2019), had extensive contact with lobbyists across all sectors as the government's chief legislative strategist
maid_position: Voted YES on Bill C-14 (2016, original MAID legislation) and YES on Bill C-7 (2021, MAID expansion).
foreign_connections: Born in Kitchener, Ontario to parents who immigrated from India in the 1970s; Sikh heritage
Listed by Indiaspora among notable Canadian government leaders of Indian heritage
No documented foreign lobbying connections or sponsored foreign travel found in publicly available records
financial_notes: No individual Ethics Commissioner sanctions found in public record separate from the broader WE Charity investigation
WE Charity contract she signed was worth up to $43.53 million in public funds
Removed from cabinet in 2021 reshuffle following WE Charity affair

name: Ginette Petitpas Taylor
current_role: MP for Moncton-Dieppe (re-elected 2025, 63%, 4th term). President of the Treasury Board (appointed 2025, continued under PM Carney). Previously served as Minister of Health (2017-2019), Minister of Official Languages (2021-2024), Minister of Veterans Affairs (2024), Minister of Employment, Workforce Development and Labour (2024).

controversies.title: Veterans Affairs and Desmond inquiry response (2024)
controversies.details: As Minister of Veterans Affairs, Petitpas Taylor responded to the Nova Scotia Desmond inquiry report (investigating why a former soldier killed three family members and himself in 2017). She admitted she had not read the full report when responding publicly. The inquiry called for systemic changes in how veterans' health records are shared between federal and provincial systems.

controversies.title: Cannabis legalization oversight as Health Minister (2017-2019)
controversies.details: As Health Minister, oversaw cannabis legalization (Bill C-45), making Canada the first G7 nation to legalize recreational cannabis. While not a personal scandal, the implementation attracted criticism over regulatory gaps and the persistence of black-market sales, which she later acknowledged.

lobbying_highlights: 317 total lobbying contacts logged in the federal Lobbyists Registration System
As Minister of Health during cannabis legalization, the Health portfolio was heavily lobbied by pharmaceutical, cannabis industry, and healthcare sector organizations
As President of Treasury Board, now oversees government spending and procurement policy, attracting lobbying from contractors and public sector unions
Lobbying registry search available at lobbycanada.gc.ca for detailed communication logs
maid_position: Voted YES on Bill C-14 (2016, original MAID legislation) and YES on Bill C-7 (2021, MAID expansion). As Health Minister (2017-2019), held the portfolio during the period between the two MAID bills.
foreign_connections: Chair of the Canada-France Inter-Parliamentary Association
Vice-Chair of the Canadian Branch of the Assemblee parlementaire de la Francophonie

name: Anthony Housefather
current_role: MP for Mount Royal (re-elected 2025, 51%, 4th term). Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Emergency Management and Community Resilience. Special Advisor on Jewish Community Relations and Antisemitism (appointed July 2024 by PM Trudeau). Chair of Canada-Israel Friendship Group. Co-founder of Inter-Parliamentary Task Force to Combat Online Antisemitism.

controversies.title: Threatened to leave Liberal caucus over Gaza ceasefire motion (2024)
controversies.details: Housefather was one of only three Liberal MPs to vote against the NDP motion calling for a ceasefire in Gaza, ending Canadian arms exports to Israel, and recognizing Palestinian statehood. He publicly stated 'a line had been crossed' and spent weeks considering leaving the Liberal Party. He ultimately decided to remain. Former public safety minister Marco Mendicino and Winnipeg MP Ben Carr also voted against the motion.

controversies.title: Highest CIJA-lobbied MP in Canada (2024)
controversies.details: According to the federal Lobbyists Registration System data analyzed by The Maple, Housefather topped the list of the 10 MPs most lobbied by CIJA (Centre for Israel and Jewish Affairs) with 67 logged contacts (average 8 per year). He then received the government-appointed role of Special Advisor on Jewish Community Relations and Antisemitism in July 2024, raising conflict-of-interest concerns from critics.

controversies.title: Special Advisor appointment drew criticism (2024)
controversies.details: His appointment as Special Advisor on Jewish Community Relations and Antisemitism was delayed by concerns about Liberal caucus divisions. Critics argued the role conflated criticism of Israel with antisemitism. The appointment drew debate in Hill Times and other outlets about whether CIJA's most-lobbied MP should hold such a role.

controversies.title: Voted against ceasing arms exports to Israel
controversies.details: Housefather voted NO on the House motion to cease arms exports to Israel during the Gaza conflict, one of a small number of Liberal MPs to do so.

lobbying_highlights: 315 total lobbying contacts logged in the federal Lobbyists Registration System (all organizations)
67 CIJA lobbying contacts specifically (highest of any MP, per The Maple analysis of registry data as of April 2024)
User-provided figure of 87 CIJA meetings may reflect a more recent or differently-scoped count from the registry
CIJA lobbied or sponsored trips for 58% of MPs running in 2025 election; Housefather is the top recipient
Chair of the Canada-Israel Friendship Group — a parliamentary association that regularly interfaces with Israeli government officials and pro-Israel lobby organizations
Co-Chair of the Inter-Parliamentary Task Force to Combat Online Antisemitism, which works alongside CIJA and the Canadian Jewish Political Affairs Committee (CJPAC)
maid_position: Voted YES on Bill C-14 (2016, original MAID legislation) and YES on Bill C-7 (2021, MAID expansion).

foreign_connections.details: Chair of Canada-Israel Friendship Group. Chair of Canada-Israel Interparliamentary Group (since 2021). Co-founder of Inter-Parliamentary Task Force to Combat Antisemitism. 67+ CIJA lobbying contacts. Previously worked with the Canadian Jewish Congress (CIJA predecessor). Publicly stated 'I will always be a strong supporter of Israel' and 'Trudeau is more pro-Israel than Harper.' Voted against Gaza ceasefire motion and against ending arms exports to Israel. Appointed Special Advisor on Jewish Community Relations and Antisemitism by PM Trudeau (July 2024).

financial_notes: CIJA has spent $678,277 on sponsored trips to Israel for 156 incumbent MPs since 2007 (58% of those running in 2025). Housefather is among the most heavily engaged with CIJA.
Proactive disclosure of travel available through ourcommons.ca
No individual Ethics Commissioner sanctions found in public record
